title: wish, hope and I'd rather
tagline: How to say you want things to be different — now, in the past, or just less annoying.
why: Wishing things were different, hoping for good news, and saying what you'd prefer are things you do every day in English, and B1 Preliminary checks you can tell wish (imaginary) apart from hope (real) in the reading cloze. Using them naturally also makes your Speaking Part 3 photo description or your Writing Part 2 story sound much more personal.

hook.text: Sofia's birthday is tomorrow. Nadia: "I wish we had more time to plan it!" Liam: "I hope she doesn't find out about the surprise." Mateo: "I'd rather bake a cake than buy one."
hook.ask: Nadia's sentence is about now (an imaginary present). Liam's sentence is a real hope for the future. What tense follows wish, and what follows hope?

diagrams.title: wish: present or past?

marks.label: Sofia didn't get a party last year

diagrams.caption: wish + past simple = a present regret. wish + past perfect = a past regret.

diagrams.title: How to complain politely with wish + would

steps.label: wish + subject + would + verb
steps.ex: I wish you would stop tapping your pen.

steps.label: use it for things that annoy you and could change
don't use wish + would about yourself
steps.ex: NOT I wish I would be taller — say I wish I were taller.

diagrams.caption: wish + would is for other people or things that bother you — not for yourself.

head: Structure
Form
Example
Meaning
rows: I wish I had a bigger room.
I wish I hadn't said that.
I hope she likes the cake.
I'd rather + verb / I'd prefer + to
if only + past simple / past perfect
If only I had more time!
a stronger, more emotional wish — no result half needed

use.point: wish + past simple: not true now

examples.text: I wish I had more free time this week.
examples.note: I don't have more time — a present regret

examples.text: Liam wishes he could sing better for the party.
examples.note: wishes + could = an imaginary present ability
were, not was, after wish — just like the second conditional

examples.text: If only I had a bike like Liam's!
examples.note: if only is a stronger version of wish — same past simple, no result half

use.point: wish + past perfect: not true in the past

examples.text: I wish I hadn't told Sofia about the surprise.
examples.note: a regret about something already done

examples.text: Nadia wishes she had bought the present earlier.
examples.note: she didn't, and now it's too late

examples.text: We wish we'd planned the party sooner.
examples.note: 'd planned = had planned, a regret about the past

examples.text: I wish Liam would stop checking his phone.
Mateo wishes his little brother would knock before coming in.
I wish it would stop raining before the party.
examples.note: about the weather, not about yourself

use.point: hope, I'd rather and I'd prefer

examples.note: a real, possible wish about now or the future

examples.text: I'd rather bake a cake than buy one.
examples.note: a preference — no to before the verb

examples.text: Nadia would prefer to keep it a secret.

watch_out.wrong: I wish I have more time.
watch_out.why: After wish about now, use the past simple, not the present.

watch_out.wrong: I wish I would be taller.
watch_out.why: Don't use wish + would about yourself — use the past simple (were).

watch_out.wrong: I wish I hadn't say that.
watch_out.why: wish + past perfect needs the past participle after hadn't.

watch_out.wrong: I hope she will likes it.
watch_out.why: hope + present simple — never double the verb form with will and -s together.
I'd rather is followed by the base verb, never to.
I'd prefer needs to before the verb — the opposite rule from I'd rather.

l1.wrong: I wish I have more time.
l1.why: Ojalá + subjunctive becomes wish + past simple in English, never the present.

l1.wrong: I wish I said it before.
l1.right: I wish I'd said it before.
l1.why: A regret about the past needs wish + past perfect (had + participle).
Espero (a real, possible wish) is hope, not wish — wish is for things that are NOT true.

l1.right: I'd rather stay home. / I'd prefer to stay home.
l1.why: Spanish prefiero needs a helper verb in English: rather + base verb or prefer + to + verb.
A wish for something annoying to change uses wish + would, not the present simple.

remember.trick: Wish means 'not true' — hope means 'maybe yes'!
remember.tip: If it's real and possible, say hope. If it's imaginary or a past regret, say wish.

can_do: I can say what I wish were different now, with wish + past simple.
I can say what I regret about the past, with wish + past perfect.
I can talk about real hopes with hope, and preferences with I'd rather / I'd prefer to.
summary: wish + past simple = something you want to be different now (I wish I had…); if only is a stronger version of the same idea.
wish + past perfect = a regret about the past (I wish I'd known…).
wish + would = you want someone or something (not yourself) to change.
hope + present/will is for real, possible wishes — the opposite feeling from wish.
I'd rather + base verb, but I'd prefer + to + verb — don't mix the two patterns.
